name: Rebalance client portfolios to their asset mix
summary: Market moves, client cash flows and private market calls and distributions pull each client portfolio away from the asset mix its board approved. Each month, and after large market moves, a total portfolio analyst calculates the portfolio's weights through its pool holdings, remaps private asset deviations to public targets and adds expected flows, and a risk analyst checks the exposures. A total portfolio manager decides whether to act and designs the cheapest fix: unit switches between pools, changes to segregated holdings, or futures and currency overlays, which pass a limit check and the head of total portfolio management before the switches are keyed and released. Stale private valuations, pool cut-offs and the need to keep several clients' switches in shared pools fair make it slower and more manual than it looks.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Five client portfolios in 2021, each with its own targets and ranges. Only public equity and public market alternatives were pooled in 2021, so rebalancing mixed unit switches with segregated trades and overlays. Overlay execution, trading and unit dealing are separate processes.

trigger: The monthly rebalancing cycle after month-end positions are reconciled, or a drift alert from daily risk monitoring after a large market move, or a new policy mix that starts a transition path.
end_state: The review is logged with either a no-action decision or completed switches, overlays and trades that put the portfolio back within its ranges and near target, and the relationship and reporting teams are told.

volume.seasonality: One review per portfolio per month, with extra reviews after sharp market moves such as March 2020.

evidence.note: Five portfolios reviewed monthly as in the organisation file; the model manager rebalanced in 2020 and cites systematic rebalancing in 2022. Extra reviews are an author estimate.

Risk analytics system (third-party factor and stress models)

steps.name: Pull positions and calculate current weights
steps.description: A total portfolio analyst pulls the client portfolio's reconciled positions from the book of record, its units in each pool with a look-through to asset classes, the latest private asset values (often a quarter old) and overlay exposures, and calculates weights against the policy targets and the current step of any transition path.

error.defect_description: A stale private value or missing pending trade distorts the weights.

evidence.note: Policies set targets and ranges by asset class, and rebalancing is systematic; data sources follow the organisation file's systems. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Remap private asset deviations to public targets
steps.description: The analyst applies the manager's remapping rules: private equity, real estate and infrastructure that sit above or below target because they cannot be traded are offset by adjusting the targets for public equities and bonds, so the client keeps roughly its intended risk.

error.defect_description: Remapping applied to the wrong asset class or with an old rule.

control.basis: Client SIP&P clause: private asset over or underweights remapped to public assets under the manager's policy (The pension client SIP&P section 4; the insurance client SIPP)

evidence.note: Remapping of private over and underweights to public assets is stated in both clients' policies. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Independently check exposures in the risk system
steps.description: A risk analyst compares the analyst's weights and drift with the risk system's daily exposures for the same portfolio and date and flags differences above a small tolerance, usually from timing of private values, pending trades or overlay exposures.

error.defect_description: A difference within tolerance hides a real error.

control.basis: Independent risk function checks exposures used for client rebalancing decisions (daily monitoring against client policy ranges)

evidence.note: The organisation file describes daily risk monitoring against client policy ranges; the check and its 10% difference rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Add expected client flows, capital calls and liquidity
steps.description: The analyst adds the client's expected contributions and withdrawals, capital calls and distributions and margin needs from the weekly liquidity forecast, so flows can be used to rebalance instead of trading and the proposal leaves enough liquid assets.

error.defect_description: A large capital call or client withdrawal is missed.

evidence.note: Liquidity is needed for benefit payments, capital calls, rebalancing and collateral, and managed to avoid forced selling. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review drift and decide whether to act
steps.description: A total portfolio manager reviews each asset class against its range and target, the cost of trading and expected flows, and decides: no action, rebalance now (outside a range or drifted past the internal trigger), or, for private assets outside their range, write a plan to reach target.

error.defect_description: A drift that should trigger action is left alone.

control.basis: Client SIP&P targets and ranges, which the IMA requires the manager to follow

evidence.note: The model manager must follow the client SIP&P; an IPS defines ranges and the response to a breach; the model manager avoids large overweights. Branch shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Design the rebalancing proposal
steps.description: The portfolio manager chooses how to move back toward target at least cost: switch units between pools, change segregated bond or money market holdings, or adjust futures and currency overlays where assets cannot be traded quickly, netting with expected client flows and with other clients' switches in the same pools.

error.defect_description: Proposal breaches a client restriction or leverage limit, or ignores another client's pending switch.

evidence.note: Futures and forwards modify exposures without trading the underlying; derivatives may be used for rebalancing; money market holdings include rebalancing strategies. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check limits, leverage and margin capacity
steps.description: A risk analyst runs the proposed trades and overlays through the client's restrictions, leverage limit and counterparty and margin capacity, and the post-trade weights through the risk system, and returns the proposal if anything breaches.

control.basis: OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 31(e): prevent investments that contravene restrictions in the client's IMA and policy

evidence.note: Control from the OSC decision; branch shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm timing and capacity with pool managers
steps.description: For a large switch the portfolio manager warns the public equity pool managers, who confirm they can invest or raise the cash in their mandates on the dealing date or ask for the switch to be spread over several days.

evidence.note: Author estimate; pool cash deployment is a separate process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Head of total portfolio management approves
steps.description: The managing director reviews the proposals for all clients together, checks consistency with the house view and fairness between clients sharing pools, and approves, amends or holds them.

control.basis: Delegated trading authority and fair treatment of clients sharing pools (OSC decision of 17 May 2017, para 31(d))

evidence.note: Fairness among members and pools required in board-approved policy; approval routine is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare unit switch instructions
steps.description: The analyst keys the approved pool switches as redemption and subscription instructions for the client account on the next dealing date in the transfer agency template.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check and release the switch instructions
steps.description: The portfolio manager checks each keyed switch against the approved proposal and releases them to transfer agency before the dealing cut-off, or sends them back.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send overlay and segregated trade requests
steps.description: The portfolio manager sends the overlay team the futures and currency changes, and the fixed income team the segregated bond or money market changes, as part of the approved proposal, with sizes and timing.

error.defect_description: Overlay size sent with the wrong sign or client.

evidence.note: Derivatives used for asset allocation; leverage applied at total portfolio level. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for dealing and execution
steps.description: The switches are dealt at the next dealing date's unit prices, overlays and segregated trades are executed by the desk, and confirmations and new unit balances arrive.

evidence.note: Daily unit pricing and business-day dealing are organisation file assumptions; timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Confirm post-rebalance weights
steps.description: The analyst recalculates the client's weights from the confirmed unit balances and executed overlays and compares them with the intended result; a residual drift from price moves or partial fills goes back for a top-up decision.

evidence.note: Author estimate; 10% top-up rate assumed.

steps.name: Record the rebalance in the log
steps.description: The analyst records the drift, decision, trades, costs and rationale in the rebalancing log used for the client's monthly report and for audit.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Tell client relationship and reporting teams
steps.description: The portfolio manager emails the relationship manager and client reporting a short note on what was rebalanced and why, including any range breaches and how they were cured, for the monthly report and client questions.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Record the no-action decision
steps.description: The analyst records that the portfolio was within its ranges and why no trade was made, with the weights, in the rebalancing log for the monthly report.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Write a plan to bring private assets back to target
steps.description: Where a private asset class sits outside its range because of valuations, calls or distributions, the portfolio manager writes a short plan: commitment pacing changes, secondary sales or purchases, and the public remapping in the meantime, for the client.

error.defect_description: Plan relies on a pacing assumption the private teams cannot meet.

control.basis: Client SIP&P: if private allocations deviate outside ranges the manager outlines its plan to reach targets (The pension client SIP&P section 4; the insurance client SIPP)

evidence.note: Both the pension client SIP&P and the insurance client SIPP state that the model manager should outline its plan to reach targets when private allocations are outside ranges. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Head reviews the plan and sends it to the relationship manager
steps.description: The managing director reviews the plan with the private markets heads, approves it and sends it to the relationship manager for the client, then the public side of the portfolio is rebalanced against the remapped targets.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Exposure differences between teams
exceptions.description: The analyst's weights and the risk system disagree because of pending trades, private valuation timing or overlay exposures, and the data must be fixed before deciding.

exceptions.name: Proposal fails the limit or capacity check
exceptions.description: A proposed overlay would breach a leverage, counterparty or margin limit, or a switch would breach a client restriction, so it is redesigned.

exceptions.name: Private asset outside its range
exceptions.description: Valuation changes, capital calls or distributions push a private asset class outside its range; the manager writes a plan to reach target and rebalances the public side against remapped targets.

exceptions.name: Large switch spread over several days
exceptions.description: A switch too large for a pool to absorb in one day is split, with the pool managers' agreement, over several dealing dates.

exceptions.name: Residual drift after execution
exceptions.description: Prices move between decision and dealing, or overlays are partly filled, and a top-up is needed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end data to logged decision or completed rebalance
benchmarks.population: Monthly client portfolio rebalancing reviews at a multi-client pooled fund manager

evidence.note: No published measure; set from one to four days to reconcile month-end positions and about a day to decide (about three to four days for a no-action review), plus a day to approve and one to three days for dealing and confirmation when trades are made (about six to nine days); half of reviews end with no action, so the median falls between the two groups. The CFA Institute example policy allows two business days to act after a range breach.

benchmarks.unit: business days to return within range (example policy)

evidence.note: Example: return the asset class to within 0 to 50% of its tolerable range no more than two business days after the breach.
Example of the width of policy ranges the review tests against.

benchmarks.population: The pension client SAA approved April 2021

evidence.note: Rebalancing follows a multi-year transition path after a new policy mix.

pain_points.description: Private assets are valued quarterly with a lag, so weights used for monthly decisions are partly stale and remapping rules have to fill the gap.

evidence.note: Private deviations allowed and remapped; non-traded assets valued at least annually and reviewed quarterly at the insurance client.

pain_points.description: Weights are built in spreadsheets from several systems (book of record, unitholder register, private markets system) and checked against the risk system, so differences must be chased before any decision.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the organisation file's systems.

pain_points.description: Each client's mix differs, so one market move creates several separate decisions, and switches by several clients in the same pool must be netted and treated fairly.

evidence.note: Fairness among members and pools required; client mixes differ widely.

pain_points.description: Unit switches can only be dealt at pool dealing points, so overlays are often used as a bridge and later unwound.

evidence.note: Futures change exposure without trading the underlying; derivatives permitted for rebalancing.

sources.title: Insurance fund: statement of investment policies and procedures (The insurance client web page)
sources.supports: The insurance client board approves the SIPP and reviews it at least once each fiscal year; detailed asset-liability study of the policy mix no less often than every four years; the model manager sole investment manager; derivatives may be used for rebalancing; liquidity coverage monitored at least monthly; performance, risk and compliance reviewed at least quarterly; policy asset mix with minimum, target and maximum by asset class; private over or underweights remapped to public assets and the model manager outlines a plan to reach targets when outside ranges; non-traded investments valued at least annually and reviewed quarterly, public investments at least monthly

assumptions: The unit is one monthly review of one client portfolio, as in the organisation file; daily drift monitoring is part of daily risk monitoring and only its alerts start a case here.
Half of monthly reviews end with no action because the portfolio is within its ranges; 42% lead to a rebalance and 8% to a plan for a private asset breach. These shares are author estimates.
Overlay execution, trading and unit dealing are separate processes; this workflow waits for their confirmations in s13.

No public source gives the manager's rebalancing thresholds, approval limits or timing; steps, times and the cycle time benchmark are author estimates checked against client policy documents and the CFA Institute example.
